hero.title: Find out how much load your database can take
hero.lead: Describe a database and a workload, and Stroppy Cloud brings up a stand in your cloud, runs the test and hands you a report: queries per second, latency and where the errors started. Compare it with earlier runs or share it as a link.

story.label: How a run goes

provision.title: A stand in your cloud
provision.body: Machines for the database and the load are created in your cloud account. The database and its data stay with you, and the cloud bills you for the machines directly.

deploy.title: The database sets itself up
deploy.body: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, YDB, CockroachDB, Picodata or OrioleDB, from one node to a cluster. Stroppy Cloud checks the stand before the load: a passing glitch gets retried on its own, and if something is really broken it stops the run and tells you what.

load.title: The load is live
load.body: While stroppy runs the scenario you see QPS, latency and errors, plus the logs and metrics of every machine, without waiting for the end.

result.title: A place in the rating, a comparison
result.body: You can send the run to the public rating, where it sits next to setups of the same sizes, and compare it with your earlier runs. By then the stand is already gone.

story.heading: How a run goes
story.sub: Here's what it looks like for PostgreSQL 17 with Patroni on three nodes: the path from the Launch button to a line in the rating.

footer.about: Database load testing with stroppy, in your own cloud.

end.title: Try it on your database
end.lead: Connect your cloud, pick a database and a scenario, and Stroppy Cloud does the rest. Not sure where to start? Take a ready example.

checks.title: Checks before the load
checks.patroni: Patroni: leader {{leader}}, both replicas in sync

rating.title: Public rating
rating.sub: Runs their authors made public. Numbers are compared only within one load scenario, and each row says what hardware produced it.
rating.emptyBody: Nothing here yet. Publish a run and it'll be the first.
